They are therefore of different moods, or they divide themselves into two parties. Therefore, he tries to influence them through prayers and obedience to their presumed will, or also through threats. Primeval man knows no real-mechanical causes at all, but only causers or originators, and even today the charcoal-burner curses his fire if it will not burn well. — One sees in the formation of myths the entire difficulty of naturally causal thinking. A change always has something very alienating. One would hardly like to believe that the sun is suddenly on the left instead of the right side. The naive human being helps himself simply with the example of his own changeable actions. He assumes, therefore, a personal conductor behind things. Either this must exist in them as their secret life, or, since this metamorphosis of the individual into a thing does sometimes fall a bit difficult, he imagines things as works and tools of secret authorities. The original inhabitant of a steppe-land, when he came to a mountain range for the first time, may have thought to himself:
